Ben / Karthik —

Draft threat-summary (concise):

Overview:
- Attack surface: multi-tenant inference path (ingest -> tokenizer -> model runtime -> KV cache -> output), control plane APIs, and optional sidecar proxies for private deployments.
- Primary risk: unintended cross-tenant disclosure via KV cache reuse, misrouted inference requests, or egress calls from runtime instances.

Key mitigations (high-level):
1) Tenant fencing and compute partitioning
   - Strong tenancy keys at request time; runtime binds KV caches with tenant-scoped namespaces and TTLs.
   - Dedicated GPU pools per-tenant for sensitive customers (configurable in Private/Dedicated).
2) Sidecar and network isolation
   - Sidecar proxies run with minimal privileges; network policies restrict outbound destinations to allowlist entries only.
   - For VPC/private deployments, optionally place inference nodes in tenant-specific subnets with ACLs.
3) Egress control and auditability
   - Outbound X-Forwarded-For strip and explicit allowlist enforcement at sidecar/outbound gateway.
   - All outbound connections generate structured audit events (request id, tenant id, destination, sha256 of payload headers). Retention policy: 90 days by default, extendable per enterprise contract.
4) KV cache hardening
   - Cache sharding by tenant id with crypto-derived keys to avoid collision; we rotate cache namespace keys on redeploys.
   - Sensitive prompt redaction and optional prompt-only in-memory caches with no disk persistence.
5) Failure modes & graceful degradation
   - If sidecar dies, runtime falls back to a quarantine mode: requests fail closed or route to an isolated fallback model depending on customer policy.
   - Control plane disconnect: local request buffering with max queue TTL and strict audit of queued requests on reconnect.

Suggested evidence to attach: tenant-fencing-matrix.xlsx (control->evidence mapping), a sample audit log snippet (included in PDF), and the annotated topology SVG.

Notes for Karthik: annotate "egress gateway" nodes and call out KMS/HSM boundary.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks again for the checklist. Please find our consolidated response below and attached evidence files. If you prefer, we can walk through this on a 30-minute call — we have availability Wed 5/14 10:30 ET (short notice) or Thu 5/15 11:00–12:00 ET.

Consolidated highlights (summary):
- Topology: Attached "redwood-topology-v2.svg" shows control plane separated from data plane. Control plane API endpoints are on a private management VPC with restricted ingress via customer-assigned CIDRs and mutual TLS. Data plane (inference runners) sit in tenant-specific subnet pools when Private deployment is selected; Hosted mode uses logical tenant namespaces with strict KV scoping.
- Tenant isolation: We bind per-request tenancy tokens to runtime sessions; KV caches are tenant-sharded with crypto-derived namespaces and ephemeral TTLs. Dedicated GPU pools are available for customers requiring physical isolation.
- KV cache protections: Sharding by tenant id, cache-key derivation, in-memory-only mode option, and no disk persistence for sensitive workloads.
- Egress controls: Outbound traffic flows through an egress gateway that enforces an allowlist of destinations and logs all attempts. Sample audit events attached; default retention 90 days (configurable).
- Threat model summary: See attached "argent-requested-evidence.pdf" (includes the 1–2 page threat summary Marissa drafted). Key mitigations focus on preventing cache collisions, restricting outbound channels, and safe-fail behaviors that close rather than expose requests under failure.

Attachments (evidence stubs):
- redwood-topology-v2.svg (annotated topology)
- tenant-fencing-matrix.xlsx (control -> evidence mapping)
- argent-requested-evidence.pdf (threat summary + sample audit snippet)
